statement:
Let $\delta_1(c)$ denote the minimum genus of a dual-separable embedding of a $c$-connected graph, and let $\gamma(K_{c+1})$ denote the genus of the complete graph $K_{c+1}$. **Optimal dual-separable embedding conjecture.** For $c \geq 8$,

$$
\delta_1(c)=\gamma(K_{c+1})+2,
$$

except when $c=11$. The paper establishes this for several small values of $c$ and for the infinite family $c=12s+4$ with $s\geq2$, but the case $c=11$ remains unresolved; the authors' evidence motivates the conjecture.
title: Optimal dual-separable embeddings of complete graphs
technical_disposition: For every c>=8 except11, equality requires both a universal genus lower bound and embedding constructions across residue classes. The known c=12s+4 family does not cover the quantifier; no full-scope construction identified.
review_scope: Literal full statement and quantifiers read; primary coverage separately specified

statement:
Let $G$ be a planar graph. An **odd coloring** of $G$ is a proper vertex coloring such that every non-isolated vertex has a color appearing an odd number of times in its neighborhood; let $\chi_o(G)$ be the minimum number of colors in such a coloring. **Petruševski–Škrekovski conjecture.** For every planar graph $G$,

$$
\chi_o(G)\leq 5.
$$

Petruševski and Škrekovski introduced odd coloring and proved that every planar graph is odd 9-colorable. The conjectured bound 5 remains open.
title: Petruševski–Škrekovski conjecture on odd colorings of planar graphs
technical_disposition: Odd5-colorability quantifies over all planar graphs and all nonisolated neighborhoods. A local recoloring must preserve every parity witness; no reducible-configuration mechanism or exact counterexample identified.
review_scope: Literal full statement and quantifiers read; primary coverage separately specified

statement:
Let $G=(V,E)$ be a graph, let $\tau(G)$ denote its covering number, and let $L(G)$ be the Laplacian matrix of $G$. For $1\leq i\leq |V|$, write $\lambda_i(L(G))$ for the $i$-th largest Laplacian eigenvalue. **Covering-number conjecture.** For all $\tau(G)\leq k\leq |V|$,

$$
\sum_{i=1}^k \lambda_i(L(G)) \leq |E|+k\cdot\tau(G)-\binom{\tau(G)}{2}.
$$

This conjecture proposes a sharper relation between Laplacian eigenvalue sums and the vertex covering number. The paper proves related bounds involving covering and matching numbers, but the displayed inequality is proposed as an open strengthening.
title: Covering-number bound for Laplacian eigenvalue sums
technical_disposition: For every vertex-cover size tau and tau<=k<=n this is a sum of the largest Laplacian eigenvalues. A trace bound natively controls only the endpoint k=n; no all-k spectral majorization bridge identified.
review_scope: Literal full statement and quantifiers read; primary coverage separately specified

statement: Let $C_{4n}$ be the cycle on $4n$ vertices, and let an **optimal extended irregular dominating labeling** mean a labeling satisfying the paper's extended irregular domination conditions with the minimum possible number of labeled vertices. **Cycle-labeling conjecture.** There exists an optimal extended irregular dominating labeling for $C_{4n}$ for every $n\geq 3$. The cases $n=1,2$ are known exceptions, and the source gives examples for $3\leq n\leq 6$; existence beyond these checked cases remains open.
title: Existence conjecture for optimal extended irregular dominating labelings of cycles
technical_disposition: All n>=3 cycle labelings require the source's extended irregular domination and optimality definitions. Small examples are not a uniform labeling construction; primary definitions remain unread.
review_scope: Literal full statement and quantifiers read; primary coverage separately specified

statement:
Let $K_n$ be the complete graph on $n$ vertices, and let $c:E(K_n)\rightarrow\{-1,+1\}$ be a **balanced colouring**, meaning that $c(K_n)=0$. Let $F$ be an $n$-vertex forest with maximum degree $\Delta$.

**Mohr–Pardey–Rautenbach conjecture.** There exists a copy $F'$ of $F$ in $K_n$ such that

$$
\left|c(F')\right|\leq \tfrac{1}{2}(\Delta-1).
$$

This conjecture asks how close to colour-balanced a spanning copy of an arbitrary forest can be in a balanced two-colouring of the complete graph. It generalises known results for perfect matchings, factors of paths, and spanning paths; its general case is presented as open in the source.
title: Mohr–Pardey–Rautenbach conjecture on almost colour-balanced spanning forests
technical_disposition: The source itself explicitly says the -1/2 additive constant fails by Hamilton-path parity (2410.06148v1 lines89). Balanced K4 and P4 give absolute sum1>1/2, reproduced on24 labeled paths. This is already in the primary, no new credit.
review_scope: Literal full statement and quantifiers read; primary coverage separately specified

statement:
Let $\mathfrak S_n$ be the set of permutations of length $n$, and let $\text{SC}_{1\underline{23}}$ be the vincular-pattern-avoiding stack-sorting map. **Second-largest-preimage conjecture.** For $n\ge 3$, the second-largest number of preimages that a permutation in $\mathfrak S_n$ can have under $\text{SC}_{1\underline{23}}$ is

$$
2^{n-3}.
$$

Moreover, exactly $2n-2$ permutations $\pi\in\mathfrak S_n$ satisfy

$$
|\text{SC}_{1\underline{23}}^{-1}(\pi)|=2^{n-3}.
$$

The maximum preimage count for this map is discussed as $2^{n-2}$; this conjecture concerns the next distinct preimage count and its multiplicity. Its resolution is not given in the supplied text.
title: Second-largest preimage conjecture for the $1\underline{23}$ stack-sorting map
technical_disposition: Source Conjecture5.2 has n>=3. Complete n5 enumeration yields second-largest fiber5 instead of4, with two such outputs instead of8 expected outputs at the proposed level. Two independent simulators and the source example agree. Small full universal refutation route; source/prior/registry gates remain.
review_scope: Literal full statement and quantifiers read; primary coverage separately specified

statement:
Let $\mathfrak S_n$ be the set of permutations of length $n$, and let $\text{SC}_{1\underline{23}}$ and $\text{SC}_{3\underline{21}}$ be the corresponding vincular-pattern-avoiding stack-sorting maps. **Unique-maximizers conjecture.** The maximum of $|\text{SC}_{1\underline{23}}^{-1}|$ is uniquely achieved by

$$
\pi=(n-1)(n-2)\cdots 1n,
$$

and the maximum of $|\text{SC}_{3\underline{21}}^{-1}|$ is uniquely achieved by

$$
\pi=23\cdots n1.
$$

The claim refines the asserted maximum preimage count $2^{n-2}$ by specifying its unique attaining permutation for each map. The supplied text presents this as a conjecture following partial smoothing results; no resolution is given.
title: Unique maximizers for the $1\underline{23}$ and $3\underline{21}$ stack-sorting maps
technical_disposition: Source Conjecture4.19 uniquely names the descending-then-n maximizer. At n8 the named output76543218 and different output65432817 both have64 preimages. Enumerating all8! inputs certifies the two counts; uniqueness at the named output cannot hold. Same stack-fiber family as365437; not separate suggested credit.
review_scope: Literal full statement and quantifiers read; primary coverage separately specified

statement:
Let $X(\Delta_{n-1})$ be the toric variety associated with a reflexive toric diagram $\Delta_{n-1}$, and let $\widetilde{X(\Delta_{n-1})}$ denote the relevant resolution. Let $V_{min}$ be the minimum volume of the corresponding Sasaki–Einstein $(2n-1)$-manifold, and let $m_n$ satisfy $m_n>m_{n+1}$. **Universal volume-bound conjecture.** For every $n$, 
$$
\frac{1}{\chi(\widetilde{X(\Delta_{n-1})})}\leq V_{min}\leq m_n\int c_1^{n-1}(\widetilde{X(\Delta_{n-1})}).
$$
 The bounds are expressed through the Euler number and the first Chern number of the associated toric variety. The paper attributes this proposed universal extension to previously studied cases $n=3$ and $4$; its validity for arbitrary $n$ remains open.
title: Universal volume bounds for reflexive toric Calabi–Yau cones
technical_disposition: For every n the toric volume comparison needs normalization of Vmin, resolution and constants mn. Neither Chern-integral computation for one cone nor dimensions3/4 proves the universal assertion; definitions and dependencies unread.
review_scope: Literal full statement and quantifiers read; primary coverage separately specified

statement:
Let $p$ and $q$ be coprime integers with $q$ odd. For the periodic problem $\Sigma(p/q)$, let $\gamma_k(p/q)$ denote the length of the gap with label $k$. **Gap-decay and extremal-frequency conjecture.** There is a constant $R$ satisfying

$$
8\ge R>3.05124276000\pm 1.56\cdot 10^{-12}
$$

such that

$$
\min_k\gamma_k(1/q)>\min_{p,k}\gamma_k(p/q)>\min_k\gamma_k(2/q)>R^{-k}.
$$

This conjecture records the numerically observed extremal behavior of the smallest periodic spectral gaps and an exponential lower bound on their decay; it was checked computationally for odd $q\le 95$, while its validity in general remains open.
title: Gap-decay and extremal-frequency conjecture for the critical almost Mathieu operator
technical_disposition: Literal min over p,k cannot be strictly greater than the p=2 minimum when p=2 is included (odd q). The displayed free k after minimization also needs correction. This is a wording/domain defect, not a substantive spectral discovery.
review_scope: Literal full statement and quantifiers read; primary coverage separately specified

statement:
Let $u$ be an element of the plactic monoid, let $m=\max u$, and let $\ell$ be the number of rows of $P(u)$. For $w\in C(u)$, write the rows of $P(w)$ as $R_i$ for $i\geq 1$.

**Strengthened row-maximum conjecture.** For every $i$ with $1\leq i\leq \ell$,

$$
\max R_i\leq m.
$$

This would strengthen the row-maximum bound used in the paper to characterize centralizers in the plactic monoid, and is presented as a direction for future research; its resolution is not established here.
title: The strengthened row-maximum conjecture for plactic centralizers
technical_disposition: For all centralizer words and each row i<=ell, inserting a large letter may alter several tableau rows. No plactic-normal-form construction respecting commutation and the row range identified; source body unread.
review_scope: Literal full statement and quantifiers read; primary coverage separately specified

statement:
Let $\mathcal{A}$ be a $k$-th order, $n$-dimensional tensor, let $lambda$ be an eigenvalue, and let

$$
\mathcal{V}_{lambda}(\mathcal{A})=ccn
$$

be its eigenvariety. Suppose that this variety has irreducible components $V_1,ldots,V_kappa$, and write $\mathrm{am}(lambda)$ for the algebraic multiplicity and $\mathrm{gm}(lambda)$ for the maximum dimension of an irreducible component. **Hu–Ye's conjecture.**

$$
\mathrm{am}(lambda) geq sum_{i=1}^{kappa} \mathrm{dim}(V_i)(k-1)^{\mathrm{dim}(V_i)-1},
$$

and, in particular,

$$
\mathrm{am}(lambda) geq \mathrm{gm}(lambda)(k-1)^{\mathrm{gm}(lambda)-1}.
$$

Hu and Ye proposed this bound in 2016 and proved it in several cases; the paper studies further cases, but the general assertion remains open.
title: Hu–Ye's eigenvariety bound for tensor eigenvalue multiplicity
technical_disposition: General tensor order and eigenvariety components require comparing resultant multiplicity to dimensions. The literal text has malformed TeX; interpreting it needs the source definition. Matrix or diagonal cases do not settle all tensors.
review_scope: Literal full statement and quantifiers read; primary coverage separately specified

statement:
Let $\alpha$ be an irrational number, and let $1<r<n$. Define a set $A$ consisting of $\lfloor n/r\rfloor$ elements from $\mathbb Q-\alpha(r-1)$ and $n-\lfloor n/r\rfloor$ elements from $\mathbb Q+\alpha$.

**Extremal construction conjecture.** The maximum number of $r$-subsets with rational sums among an $n$-element set of irrational numbers is attained by this construction. The paper has determined the corresponding maximum in several ranges, but leaves the range $4\leq r<n/2$ open; this conjecture proposes the stated construction as extremal for all $1<r<n$.
title: The two-equivalence-class extremal construction conjecture for rational-value sums
technical_disposition: All1<r<n rational-sum extremality includes the hard4<=r<n/2 range. Counting the proposed two-class construction only gives a lower bound; no upper bound across arbitrary irrational equivalence classes identified.
review_scope: Literal full statement and quantifiers read; primary coverage separately specified

statement:
Let $H$ be a graph with $m$ edges and no isolated vertices. Let $\varepsilon>0$ and let $C_0$ be a positive constant depending on $H$ and $\varepsilon$.

**Pavez-Signé's conjecture.** For all $C\geq C_0$ and any integer $m$, if $G$ is a graph on $n\geq Cm$ vertices with minimum degree at least $(1/2+\varepsilon)n$, then $G$ contains a spanning $H$-subdivision.

This conjecture was raised by Pavez-Signé and is settled in the source paper in a stronger form for digraphs with minimum in- and out-degree at least $n/2$.
title: Pavez-Signé's spanning subdivision conjecture
technical_disposition: The literal statement itself reports a stronger digraph theorem settles this question. Source theorem proof not read, so no audited retirement; no new-result investment. Quantifier m is also used twice and needs source reconciliation.
review_scope: Literal full statement and quantifiers read; primary coverage separately specified

statement:
Let $H$ be a digraph with minimum degree $\delta(H)\geq 1$. Let $D$ be a digraph of order $n$, and for vertices $u,v\in V(D)$ with $uv\notin A(D)$ consider the degree-sum condition $d_D^+(u)+d_D^-(v)\geq n+C_H$.

**Spanning subdivision conjecture.** There is a constant $n_0$ and a real number $C_H$ depending only on $H$ such that, whenever $D$ has order $n$ and the displayed condition holds for every non-edge $uv$, $D$ contains a spanning $H$-subdivision.

This is posed as a problem for sparser digraphs than those covered by the main dense-digraph results. The source gives no resolution of this proposed statement, so its status remains open.
title: The spanning subdivision conjecture for digraphs under non-edge degree-sum conditions
technical_disposition: For each fixed digraph H, n0 and CH must force a spanning subdivision under every nonedge degree-sum constraint. Dense minimum-degree results do not directly cover this Ore-type condition; no bounded full mechanism identified.
review_scope: Literal full statement and quantifiers read; primary coverage separately specified

statement:
For integers $n\geq r\geq 2$, a fractional $(r-1,r,n)$-Steiner system in an $r$-uniform hypergraph $H$ is a function $\varphi:E(H)\to\mathbb{R}_{\geq0}$ such that $\deg_H^\varphi(p)=1$ for every $(r-1)$-set $p\in V(H)^{(r-1)}$. **Fractional Steiner-system threshold conjecture.** The minimum codegree threshold for a fractional $(r-1,r,n)$-Steiner system is

$$
\frac{(r-1)n}{r}+\Theta(1).
$$

This generalizes the paper's parity-based lower-bound construction and asks for the asymptotically sharp fractional codegree threshold; it remains open.
title: The conjectured fractional codegree threshold for generalized Steiner systems
technical_disposition: All uniformities r and large n require sharp fractional codegree threshold through LP feasibility. The parity lower-bound construction is not the upper-bound certificate; no general dual obstruction classification identified.
review_scope: Literal full statement and quantifiers read; primary coverage separately specified

statement:
Let $\mathcal{C}^{(2)}_{n,5}$ be the closure of the image of the rational map

$$
\mathcal{V}_{2,n,5} \dashrightarrow \mathbb{P}^{\binom{n}{2}-1}
$$

whose coordinates are given by the conformal two-point functions

$$
\frac{H_{ij}}{P_{ij}^3}=\frac{(W_i\cdot W_j)(P_i\cdot P_j)-(W_i\cdot P_j)(W_j\cdot P_i)}{(P_i\cdot P_j)^3},\qquad 1\leq i<j\leq n.
$$

**Dimension conjecture.** The dimension of the two-point variety is

$$
\dim \mathcal{C}^{(2)}_{n,5}=\min\left(5n-11,\binom{n}{2}-1\right).
$$

This computationally observed formula predicts the dimension of the variety of conformal two-point correlators as the minimum of the expected parameter count and the dimension of the ambient projective space; its general validity remains to be established.
title: Dimension conjecture for the conformal two-point variety
technical_disposition: All n dimension formula requires rank upper and generic attainment lower bounds for the conformal rational map. A finite Jacobian rank check could only certify fixed n; no inductive minors or rigidity mechanism identified.
review_scope: Literal full statement and quantifiers read; primary coverage separately specified

statement:
Let $V_L$ be the lattice vertex operator algebra associated with the 128-dimensional Barnes–Wall lattice, and let $E(7)$ act on $V_L$. A holomorphic conformal field theory has central charge $c$ equal to its central charge as a VOA, and its gap is the smallest positive conformal weight of a primary state.
**Holomorphic-orbifold conjecture.** The holomorphic $E(7)$-orbifold of the 128-dimensional Barnes–Wall lattice VOA exists. It is a holomorphic CFT of central charge $c=128$ with gap 4.
Such an orbifold would provide a holomorphic CFT with a large spectral gap. The claim relies on the preceding evidence that the anomaly vanishes for $m=7$ and on the resulting character computation, but remains unproved.
title: Existence of the holomorphic E(7)-orbifold of the Barnes–Wall lattice VOA
technical_disposition: Existence of the E(7) orbifold and exact gap4 needs anomaly trivialization and VOA construction, not just a plausible character. A formal dependency chain is large and no small certificate route identified.
review_scope: Literal full statement and quantifiers read; primary coverage separately specified

statement:
Let $\alpha(t)$ be the smallest number of vertices of a planar simple graph with exactly $t$ spanning trees. The known lower bound is $\alpha(t)=\Omega(\log t)$, and Stong proved $\alpha(t)=O\big((\log t)^{3/2}/\log\log t\big)$. **Logarithmic upper-bound conjecture.** For all integers $t\geq 3$, 

$$
\alpha(t)=O(\log t).
$$

This would match the lower bound and is equivalent to constructing planar simple graphs with $t$ spanning trees using only logarithmically many vertices. The conjecture remains open, although it holds for a positive proportion of $t$.
title: The logarithmic upper-bound conjecture for planar spanning-tree numbers
technical_disposition: Every integer t>=3 needs a planar simple graph with t spanning trees and O(log t) vertices. Series-parallel addition/multiplication may have large digit cost; no uniform efficient arithmetic encoding identified.
review_scope: Literal full statement and quantifiers read; primary coverage separately specified

statement: Let $\operatorname{tsat}(n,K_r,t)$ denote the minimum number of edges in a twin-free $K_r$-saturated graph on $n$ vertices with minimum degree at least $t$. A vertex is **conical** if it is adjacent to every other vertex. **Minimum-degree conical-vertex conjecture.** For all integers $r\geq 4$ and $t\geq r-2$, every extremal graph for $\operatorname{tsat}(n,K_r,t)$ has a conical vertex for large enough $n$. This is the minimum-degree analogue of the preceding conjecture and concerns the structure of extremal graphs.
title: Conical-vertex conjecture for minimum-degree twin-free saturated graphs
technical_disposition: All fixed r>=4,t>=r-2 and sufficiently large n require conical vertices in every twin-free saturation extremizer. Small graphs cannot refute eventuality; no infinite extremal nonconical family or stability proof identified.
review_scope: Literal full statement and quantifiers read; primary coverage separately specified

statement: For integers $r\geq 3$, $t\geq r-2$, and $m\geq 0$, let $s_{r,t}(m)$ be the maximum size of the family in an $(r,t)$-system $(H,\mathcal{F})$ with $|H|=m$. An extremal system is one attaining this maximum, and a vertex is **conical** if it is adjacent to every other vertex of its underlying graph. **Set-system conical-vertex conjecture.** For all integers $r\geq 4$ and $t\geq r-2$, every underlying graph of an extremal system for $s_{r,t}(m)$ has a conical vertex for large enough $m$. This predicts that extremal systems for the set-function problem inherit the recursive conical structure found in the graph formulation.
title: Conical-vertex conjecture for extremal uniform set systems
technical_disposition: All r>=4,t>=r-2 and large m concern extremal (r,t)-systems. A graph extremizer is not automatically a set-system extremizer; source system axioms unread, no infinite family route.
review_scope: Literal full statement and quantifiers read; primary coverage separately specified

statement: For integers $r\geq 3$ and $t\geq r$, let $e_{r,t}(s)$ and $e_{r,t}'(s)$ be the minimum number of edges in the underlying graph of an $(r,t)$-system and a maximal $(r,t)$-system, respectively, with family size $s$. An extremal system is one attaining the relevant minimum, and a vertex is **conical** if it is adjacent to every other vertex of its underlying graph. **Edge-system conical-vertex conjecture.** For all integers $r\geq 4$ and $t\geq r$, every underlying graph of an extremal system for $e_{r,t}(s)$ or $e_{r,t}'(s)$ has a conical vertex for large enough $s$. This predicts a conical structure for both edge-minimization problems, with and without maximality.
title: Conical-vertex conjecture for extremal edge-minimizing systems
technical_disposition: Both ordinary and maximal edge-minimizing systems for all r>=4,t>=r and large s need a conical vertex. The two optimization classes require separate optimality witnesses; no full-scope construction identified.
review_scope: Literal full statement and quantifiers read; primary coverage separately specified

statement:
Let $D\in\mathbb{N}$. An $(n,d,\lambda)$-graph is a graph on $n$ vertices with degree $d$ and second eigenvalue bounded by $\lambda$. Let $T$ be a tree of maximum degree at most $D$, and let

$$
V(T)=T_1\cup\cdots\cup T_\ell
$$

be a partition with $|T_i|\leq \alpha n$ for every $i\in[\ell]$. **Partition-injective tree homomorphism conjecture.** For every $D\in\mathbb{N}$, there exist $d\in\mathbb{N}$ and $\alpha>0$ such that, whenever $G$ is an $(n,d,\lambda)$-graph with $\lambda=\Theta(\sqrt d)$, every such tree $T$ admits a homomorphism $\phi\colon T\to G$ whose restriction to each $T_i$ is injective. If true, this would replace the use of the random branching-walk lemma in the proof of the paper's universal-hypergraph theorem and yield the optimal bound $O(n^{r-r/d})$.
title: Optimal universal hypergraph conjecture for partition-injective tree homomorphisms
technical_disposition: For every D the existence of d,alpha is uniform over host expanders, trees and partitions. A tree homomorphism alone does not ensure injectivity within arbitrary parts; no local-lemma or constructive all-part bound identified.
review_scope: Literal full statement and quantifiers read; primary coverage separately specified

statement:
Let $\underline{\delta}_9$ be the stated candidate value for the minimum dilatation of pseudo-Anosov braids with 9 strands, and let $x$ denote the variable in its defining polynomial. **10-strand minimum-dilatation conjecture.** The minimum dilatation among pseudo-Anosov braids with 10 strands equals

$$
\underline{\delta}_9=\left|x^9-2x^5-2x^4+1\right|.
$$

This revises Venzke's conjecture in the case $n=10$, after the original prediction was shown to fail there. The remaining values of $\delta_n$ are presented as an outstanding computational problem in the source.
title: Revised minimum-dilatation conjecture for 10-strand pseudo-Anosov braids
technical_disposition: The literal candidate dilatation is written as an absolute value of a polynomial rather than a specified root; source reconciliation is necessary. Enumerating10-strand braid representatives without a universal lower bound would not prove minimality.
review_scope: Literal full statement and quantifiers read; primary coverage separately specified

statement: Let $G$ be a graph with edge ideal $I(G)$. Suppose that, for some integer $q\in\mathbb{N}$, $I(G)^q$ has linear quotients with an ordering $\mathcal N^{(q)}:u_1>\dots>u_r$ of its generators. Recursively construct the **efficient ordering** $\mathcal N^{(s)}$ from $\mathcal N^{(q)}$ as defined in the source. **Efficient-ordering conjecture.** Then $I(G)^s$ has linear quotients with the efficient ordering $\mathcal N^{(s)}$ for every integer $s\geq q$. This is a refinement of the persistence conjecture because it specifies the ordering intended to provide linear quotients at every higher power; it remains open.
title: Efficient-ordering conjecture for powers of edge ideals
technical_disposition: Given a q-power efficient ordering, every higher power must have linear quotients in the recursively specified order. Finite monomial colon computations would only test bounded powers; no persistence induction controlling generators identified.
review_scope: Literal full statement and quantifiers read; primary coverage separately specified

statement:
Let $G$ be a $3$-uniform hypergraph, let $\delta_2(G)$ denote its minimum codegree, and let a square of a tight Hamilton cycle be the corresponding hypergraph power.

**Pósa-type conjecture for triple systems.** For every $\varepsilon>0$, there is $n_0$ such that every $3$-uniform hypergraph $G$ of order $n\geq n_0$ satisfying

$$
\delta_2(G)\geq (3/4+\varepsilon)n
$$

contains a square of a tight Hamilton cycle.

A relative minimum codegree slightly above $4/5$ is known to suffice, while $3/4$ is known to be necessary; proving the conjectured threshold remains open.
title: Pósa's conjecture for squares of Hamilton cycles in triple systems
technical_disposition: Every epsilon>0 and sufficiently large3-graph at codegree(3/4+epsilon)n requires a spanning squared tight cycle. Absorption and connecting lemmas would be substantial; no small exact universal certificate route.
review_scope: Literal full statement and quantifiers read; primary coverage separately specified

statement:
Let $G$ be a $3$-uniform hypergraph, let $\delta_2(G)$ denote its minimum codegree, and let $K_4(G)$ be the $4$-clique $3$-graph of $G$. A $3$-graph is **tightly connected** when any two edges can be joined by a sequence of edges in which consecutive edges overlap in two vertices.

**4-clique connectivity conjecture.** For every $\varepsilon>0$, there is $n_0$ such that every $3$-uniform hypergraph $G$ of order $n\geq n_0$ satisfying

$$
\delta_2(G)\geq (3/4+\varepsilon)n
$$

has tightly connected $K_4(G)$.

This is presented as a first step toward the conjectured square-Hamilton-cycle threshold and remains open.
title: Tight connectivity of the 4-clique graph in dense triple systems
technical_disposition: Same asymptotic density quantifiers but only tight connectivity of the4-clique3-graph. A component barrier near3/4 is plausible, but epsilon above threshold forbids simple balanced barriers; no strict-density counterfamily identified.
review_scope: Literal full statement and quantifiers read; primary coverage separately specified

statement:
Let $X$ be a connected topological space. A nonzero element $x\in H^k(X;\mathbb{Z}_2)$ **induces periodicity** if multiplication by $x$ gives isomorphisms

$$
H^i(X;\mathbb{Z}_2)\longrightarrow H^{i+k}(X;\mathbb{Z}_2)
$$

for all $i\geq 0$; in this case $H^*(X;\mathbb{Z}_2)$ is $k$-periodic. The minimum period is the least such $k\geq 1$. **The $\mathbb{Z}_2$ periodicity conjecture.** If $H^*(X;\mathbb{Z}_2)$ is $k$-periodic and $k$ is the minimum period, then $k\in\{1,2,4\}$. This conjecture extends Adams' theorem from singly generated cohomology to periodic cohomology. It is known that the minimum period is a power of two, but the restriction to $1$, $2$, or $4$ remains open.
title: The Z_2 periodicity conjecture
technical_disposition: All connected spaces with minimum mod2 cohomological period must have period1,2,4. A graded ring example requires topological realizability and Steenrod constraints; abstract algebra alone does not refute the statement.
review_scope: Literal full statement and quantifiers read; primary coverage separately specified

statement: Let $X^n$ be a space and let $p$ be a prime. Say that $H^*(X;\mathbb{Z}_p)$ is $k$-periodic up to degree $c$ when multiplication by a periodicity element induces successive isomorphisms through the last one landing in degree $c$. Assume that $k$ is the minimum period and that $0\leq m<k$ is the maximum degree with $H^m(X;\mathbb{Z}_2)\neq 0$. **The truncated periodicity conjecture.** If $p=2$ and $c\geq 2k+m$, then $k\in\{1,2,4\}$ or $(k,c)=(8,16+m)$. If $p\geq 3$ and $c\geq pk+m$, then $k=2\lambda$ for some divisor $\lambda$ of $p-1$. These are proposed truncated analogues of the periodicity conjectures; the source presents them as suggestions, and no resolution is given.
title: The Z_p periodicity conjecture in the truncated case
technical_disposition: Both p2 exceptional(k,c) and odd-prime divisor cases require truncated periodicity definitions and nonvanishing m convention. No realization theorem or all-space cohomology-operation route; literal m uses mod2 even in odd-prime branch.
review_scope: Literal full statement and quantifiers read; primary coverage separately specified

statement:
Let $G$ be a graph on $n$ vertices, and let $P^{*}_{DP}(G,k)$ denote its dual DP color function, the maximum number of colorings over all full $k$-fold covers of $G$. **Dual-DP Shameful inequality conjecture.** For every $n$-vertex graph $G$ and every $k\in\mathbb{N}$ satisfying $k\geq n-1$, 
$$
\frac{P^{*}_{DP}(G,k+1)}{(k+1)^n}\geq\frac{P^{*}_{DP}(G,k)}{k^n}.
$$
 The text motivates this as an expected extension of the Shameful inequality: it notes counterexamples for smaller values of $k$, while giving no resolution of the stated range, so the conjecture is open.
title: Dual-DP Shameful inequality conjecture
technical_disposition: For every graph and every k>=n-1, normalized maximal DP-cover coloring counts must increase. Restricting an optimal(k+1)-cover does not directly compare maxima in the needed direction; no full-scope averaging inequality identified.
review_scope: Literal full statement and quantifiers read; primary coverage separately specified

statement:
Let $(X,\delta)$ be an ordinal space with $|X|=n$, and let $\mathbf B_X$ denote its set of balls. Assume that

$$
\delta(x,y)\neq\delta(z,w)
$$

for every different pairs of points $\{x,y\}\neq\{z,w\}$ with $x\neq y$ and $z\neq w$. **Minimal ball-number conjecture.** The following inequality holds:

$$
\frac{n(n+1)}{2}\leqslant |\mathbf B_X|.
$$

Equality holds if and only if the Hasse diagram $\mathcal H(X)$ has the structure depicted in Figure 2. Without the distinct-distance restriction, the paper notes that the minimum is trivially $|X|+1$ when $|X|>1$; the restricted lower bound and its equality characterization are presented as a conjecture, with no resolution supplied.
title: The minimal ball-number conjecture for finite ordinal spaces
technical_disposition: Source Conjecture6.3 lower bound fails for a four-point ordinal space with six distinct distances and exactly9 balls<10. Two exact enumerations agree. The universal inequality is refuted without needing the equality-Hasse characterization; source/prior/registry clearance remains HOLD.

statement:
A **tournament** is an orientation of a complete graph. For an oriented graph $H$, its oriented Ramsey number, denoted by $\overrightarrow{r}(H)$, is the smallest integer $N$ such that every tournament on $N$ vertices contains a copy of $H$. For $3\leq i\leq n$, let $H(n,i)$ be the oriented graph with vertex set $\{1,2,\ldots,n\}$ and arc set

$$
\{(1,i),(j,j+1)\colon 1\leq j\leq n-1\}.
$$

**Sós's conjecture.** For each $n$ and each $i$ satisfying $4\leq i\leq n-1$,

$$
\overrightarrow{r}(H(n,i))=n.
$$

The conjecture asks when a sparse oriented graph has oriented Ramsey number equal to its order. The source attributes it to Sós, posed at the Sixth Yugoslav Seminar on Graph Theory in 1986, and gives no resolution of the full statement.
title: Sós's oriented Ramsey conjecture for the graphs H(n,i)
technical_disposition: All n and4<=i<=n-1 tournaments must contain the path-plus-chord. Hamilton paths alone do not force the specific forward chord; no rotation argument preserving chord position identified.

statement:
Let $G$ be a graph, and let $r_{K_s}(t_1,t_2)$ denote the minimum number of copies of $K_s$ in a graph that is $(t_1,t_2)$-Ramsey. Let $r(t_1,t_2)$ be the Ramsey number, the smallest $n$ such that $K_n$ is $(t_1,t_2)$-Ramsey. **Off-diagonal $F$-Ramsey conjecture.** For all positive integers $s,t_1,t_2$ satisfying $s\leq\max(t_1,t_2)$,

$$
r_{K_s}(t_1,t_2)=\binom{r(t_1,t_2)}{s}.
$$

This is the natural off-diagonal extension of the diagonal conjecture. The paper establishes the equality up to a lower-order term in the exponent when $t_1$ is $3$ or $4$, using constructions related to the asymptotics of $r(4,t)$; the full equality remains open.
title: The off-diagonal $F$-Ramsey conjecture
technical_disposition: Every s,t1,t2 requires an exact clique-count Ramsey lower bound. Exact ordinary Ramsey numbers are themselves hard in general; no counterexample with certified Ramsey property and too few cliques identified.

statement:
Let $P=\mathbb{C}[x,y,z]$ with weights $\operatorname{wt}(x)=1$, $\operatorname{wt}(y)=2$, and $\operatorname{wt}(z)=3$, and let $m\bsin\mathbb{N}_{>0}$. Set

$$
R=\mathbb{C}[x,y,z]/(x,y)^{3m-2},\qquad M=(x,y,z)^{3m-2}/(x,y)^{3m-2}.
$$

For a general $\operatorname{wt}$-homogeneous polynomial $f\bsin P$ of weight $3m$, multiplication by $f$ induces a vector-space map

$$
f\cdot:R_w\longrightarrow M_{w+3m}.
$$

**Equivalent formulation.** The map $f\cdot:R_w\to M_{w+3m}$ is an isomorphism for every $w\bsin\mathbb{N}$. This is presented as an equivalent linear-algebraic formulation of the weighted initial-ideal conjecture. It is intended to imply the primitive-multiple-line construction and hence the relevant maximum-genus cases; the source gives no resolution.
title: Equivalent linear-algebraic formulation of the weighted initial-ideal conjecture
technical_disposition: All m>0 and all weight degrees need a generic multiplication isomorphism. A chosen f at bounded m only verifies a parameter instance; no all-m leading-monomial matching or determinant noncancellation identified.

statement:
For positive integers $h$ and $k$, define

$$
S(h,k):=\sum_{j=1}^{k-1}(-1)^{j+1+\lfloor hj/k\rfloor},
$$

where $\lfloor x\rfloor$ is the greatest integer less than or equal to $x$, and define

$$
S(k):=\sum_{h=1}^{k-1}S(h,k).
$$

**Stronger linear lower-bound conjecture.** For each prime $k>3119$,

$$
S(k)>3k.
$$

This is a further numerical strengthening of the preceding lower bound. The source reports that the primes up to $10000$ failing $S(k)<3k$ have largest value $3119$, but gives no proof of the conjecture.
title: Stronger linear lower-bound conjecture for the theta-function arithmetic sum
technical_disposition: For each prime k>3119, source asks S(k)>3k. Source Section6 explicitly records unsuccessful residue-distribution bounds; elementary floor estimates remain below the required linear constant. No uniform prime bound or counterexample route; no further sweep.

statement:
Let $G$ be a tree, and let

$$
I_G(t)=i_0+i_1t+\cdots+i_{\alpha(G)}t^{\alpha(G)}
$$

be its **independence polynomial**, where $\alpha(G)$ is the maximum size of an independent set in $G$ and $i_j$ counts the independent sets of $G$ of cardinality $j$. A polynomial $I_G(t)$ of degree $d$ is **unimodal** if there is an index $0\leq j\leq d$ such that

$$
i_0\leq\cdots\leq i_{j-1}\leq i_j\geq i_{j+1}\geq\cdots\geq i_d.
$$

**Alavi–Malde–Schwenk–Erdős conjecture.** The independence polynomial of every tree is unimodal.

The conjecture was proposed in 1987. The paper establishes log-concavity, and hence unimodality, for spiders and pineapple graphs, providing further evidence, but the general tree case remains open in the supplied context.
title: Alavi–Malde–Schwenk–Erdős unimodality conjecture for independence polynomials of trees
technical_disposition: Every tree's independence polynomial requires unimodality. The tree recurrence combines polynomials with displaced peaks, so local log-concavity arguments for spiders do not extend automatically; no certified nonunimodal tree identified.

statement:
For a rectilinear drawing of the complete graph $K_n$, let $e_k(K_n)$ denote the number of edges crossed exactly $k$ times, and let

$$
\overline\max\ e_k(K_n)
$$

denote the maximum of $e_k(K_n)$ over all rectilinear drawings of $K_n$. **Sublinear crossing-profile conjecture.** For every $n\geq 1$ and $k\geq 1$,

$$
\overline\max\ e_k(K_n)=o(n\sqrt{k}).
$$

More precisely, for every $\epsilon>0$ there exists a constant $N$ such that if $n$ and $k$ are larger than $N$, then $\overline\max\ e_k(K_n)/(n\sqrt{k})<\epsilon$. The paper establishes the bounds $\Omega(n)\leq\overline\max\ e_k(K_n)\leq O(n\sqrt{k})$ in the stated range, and this conjecture proposes that the upper bound is asymptotically non-sharp.
title: The sublinear upper-bound conjecture for the crossing profile of complete graphs
technical_disposition: Both n and k tend past a shared N in the little-o quantifier. A fixed-k linear construction cannot refute this simultaneous asymptotic; no two-parameter extremal construction maintaining constant normalized ratio identified.

statement:
Let $C_5$ denote the cycle on five vertices, and let $rsat(n,C_5)$ be its rainbow saturation number. **Eventual exact rainbow saturation conjecture for $C_5$.** There exists $N_0\in\mathbb{N}$ such that, for every $n\geq N_0$,

$$
rsat(n,C_5)=2n-6.
$$

This asserts that the paper's construction for $C_5$ is eventually optimal, making its upper bound the exact value for all sufficiently large orders. The statement is presented as a belief following the paper's bounds; no resolution is supplied.
title: Eventual exact rainbow saturation conjecture for $C_5$
technical_disposition: Eventual exact2n-6 rainbow saturation ofC5 needs a universal lower bound and source saturation convention for colors. A smaller construction at finite n cannot refute eventuality; no infinite lower-construction route identified.

statement:
Let $K_n$ be the complete graph on $n$ vertices, and let $K_t$ be the complete graph on $t$ vertices. The function $L(K_n,K_t)$ denotes the minimum number of moves required for player $P_1$ to establish a copy of $K_t$ in the strong Ramsey game on $K_n$, regardless of $P_2$'s play.

**Beck's conjecture.** For sufficiently large $n$ and every integer $t\geq 3$, there is a constant $c_t$, depending only on $t$, such that

$$
L(K_n,K_t)\leq c_t.
$$

This conjecture asks whether player $P_1$ can always win in a number of moves bounded independently of the board size. Beck identified it as a major open problem, even for $t=5$.
title: Beck's bounded-move conjecture for strong Ramsey games
technical_disposition: Each fixed t needs a board-size-independent winning time. Small strong Ramsey game searches do not settle t5 or all t; no bounded forcing strategy identified.

statement:
Let $\Gamma$ be a conical grid of order $n$. The covering number with multiplicity $k$ is the minimum number of lines required to cover every point of $\Gamma$ at least $k$ times. **Conical-grid covering conjecture.** The minimum number of lines required to cover every point in $\Gamma$ at least $k$ times is at least

$$
\frac{2nk}{3}-O(k).
$$

The conjecture asserts that the lower bound known for structured triangular grids also holds for arbitrary conical grids, and is tight for fixed $n$ as $k\to\infty$ according to the surrounding discussion. No proof or disproof is supplied here.
title: The lower-bound conjecture for covering conical grids
technical_disposition: Every conical grid and covering multiplicity k requires2nk/3-O(k). A valid obstruction must respect the source grid geometry and uniform error convention; fractional covering LP for one grid is not a universal lower bound.

statement:
Let $G$ be a definably compact group defined over $\mathbb{C}((t))$. Write $G^0$ for the connected component and $G^{00}$ for the smallest type-definable subgroup of bounded index.

**Conjecture on definably compact groups.** The group $G$ is generically stable, and

$$
G^{00}=G^0
$$

is a finite-index subgroup of $G$.

This is the revised conjecture attributed in the source to the work cited as cite{LY}; the source provides no resolution evidence.
title: Generic stability and connected-component equality for definably compact groups over the Laurent series field
technical_disposition: Every definably compact group overC((t)) must be generically stable with finite-indexG00=G0. This needs model-theoretic compactness and definability machinery; no small algebraic example addressing these exact notions identified.

statement:
Let $G$ be a group definable in $\mathbb{C}((t))$. Write $G^0$ for the connected component and $G^{00}$ for the smallest type-definable subgroup of bounded index.

**Connected-component conjecture.** One has

$$
G^0=G^{00}.
$$

Consequently, $G$ is virtually an open subgroup of an algebraic group over $\mathbb{C}((t))$.

The source presents this as a conjecture and compares the consequence with Corollary 4.3 of the work cited as JY-2; no resolution is supplied.
title: Equality of connected components and bounded-index components over $\mathbb{C}((t))$
technical_disposition: All definable groups overC((t)) require equality of connected components and bounded-index components. Compact-group results would only cover a subclass; no universal reduction or definable counterexample identified.

statement:
Let $(d_1,\ldots,d_c;a_0,\ldots,a_n)$ be an $h$-regular pair, and assume $c\leq n$ and $a_i\nmid h$ for every $i$. Let $F^h(a_0,\ldots,a_n)$ denote the $\frac{1}{h}$-Frobenius number, namely the largest multiple of $h$ not representable as a nonnegative integer combination of the weights.

**Generalized Frobenius conjecture.** Then

$$
\delta(d;a)\geq F^h(a_0,\ldots,a_n).
$$

For $h=1$, this specializes to the regular-pair Frobenius conjecture attributed to Tasin. The source introduces this as the generalization to $h$-regular pairs; its resolution is not stated, so the conjecture remains open.
title: Generalized Frobenius bound for h-regular pairs
technical_disposition: All h-regular pairs with c<=n and ai not dividing h require delta>=Fh. Testing numerical semigroups needs the full h-regular divisibility condition and delta definition; those primary definitions unread, so no valid small witness inferred.

statement:
For a graph $G$ and a graph $F$, let $\mathrm{ex^*}(G,F)$ be the maximum number of edges in a subgraph of $G$ that has a proper edge-coloring with no rainbow copy of $F$. The $n$-dimensional hypercube $Q_n$ has vertex set $\{0,1\}^n$, with two vertices adjacent when they differ in exactly one coordinate. **Rainbow Erdős–Sós conjecture for hypercubes.** For each $n\in\mathbb{N}$, 

$$
\mathrm{ex^*}(Q_n,T)=\mathrm{ex^*}(Q_n,K_{1,k})
$$

for all trees $T$ on $k$ edges; equivalently, $Q_n$ satisfies the host-graph version of the rainbow Erdős–Sós question. This conjecture proposes that the rainbow extremal number on the hypercube depends only on the number of edges in the forbidden tree. The supplied text gives no resolution.
title: Rainbow Erdős–Sós conjecture for hypercubes
technical_disposition: All n and all k-edge trees compare rainbow hypercube extremal numbers with the star. Structure-dependent proper edge colorings can defeat naive greedy tree embedding; no full-scope extremal comparison identified.

statement:
For a graph $G$ and a graph $F$, let $\delta^*(G,F)$ be the maximum minimum degree of a subgraph $H\subset G$ that has a proper edge-coloring with no rainbow copy of $F$. Let $Q_n$ denote the $n$-dimensional hypercube, and let $T$ be a tree with $k$ edges. **Rainbow minimum-degree Erdős–Sós conjecture for hypercubes.** 

$$
\delta^*(Q_n,T)=k-1
$$

for all trees $T$ on $k$ edges. This is proposed as an alternative to complete graphs, where the corresponding rainbow minimum-degree quantity can depend on the structure of the tree. The supplied text gives no resolution.
title: Rainbow minimum-degree Erdős–Sós conjecture for hypercubes
technical_disposition: Literal equalitydelta*=k-1 for all hypercubes requires a relation between n and k; alwaysdelta*<=n, so n<k-1 contradicts it. This is an omitted-domain issue, not credited refutation; intended source range unread.

statement:
Let $d_{\text{T}}(n)$ denote the delay and $M_{\text{T}}(n)$ the maximum excursion of the Collatz sequence starting at the positive integer $n$. **Delay and maximum-excursion bound conjecture.** There exist positive reals $\alpha$ and $\beta$ such that, for every integer $n\geq2$, 
$$
d_{\text{T}}(n)\leq\alpha\,\log n
$$
 and 
$$
M_{\text{T}}(n)\leq n^\beta.
$$
 These weak bounds are proposed as heuristic formulations sufficient for the paper's purpose; no resolution is supplied.
title: Logarithmic delay and polynomial maximum-excursion bounds for Collatz sequences
technical_disposition: Universal logarithmic delay and polynomial maximum excursion entail finite stopping for every positive Collatz input. Finite trajectories cannot establish this; no full-scope stopping mechanism, parked as hard.

statement:
A finite set of points in the plane is in general position if no three points are collinear, and it is in convex position if its points are the vertices of a convex polygon. Let $ES(n)$ be the smallest integer $N$ such that every set of at least $N$ points in general position contains $n$ points in convex position. **Erd6s–Szekeres conjecture.** For every integer $n\geq2$,

$$
ES(n)=2^{n-2}+1.
$$

The Erd6s–Szekeres theorem guarantees that $ES(n)$ is finite, while the source records the upper bound $ES(n)\leq\binom{2n-4}{n-2}+1$. Determining the exact value remains open and is the classical Happy Ending Problem.
title: Erd6s–Szekeres conjecture for the convex-position function
technical_disposition: ExactES(n)=2^(n-2)+1 for every n is the classical global extremal problem. Small n or asymptotic upper bounds do not settle exact values; no new full-scope geometric mechanism identified.

statement:
Let $\Gamma_1$ and $\Gamma_2$ be graphs, let $\Gamma_1\square\Gamma_2$ denote their Cartesian product, and let $\mathrm{pmd}(\Gamma)$ denote the positive matching decomposition number. **Additive lower-bound conjecture for positive matching decomposition numbers.** There exists a constant $c>0$ such that

$$
\mathrm{pmd}(\Gamma_1)+\mathrm{pmd}(\Gamma_2)\leq\mathrm{pmd}(\Gamma_1\square\Gamma_2)+c
$$

for all graphs $\Gamma_1$ and $\Gamma_2$. The paper notes that its results primarily give upper bounds, while the available general lower bound is only through maximum valency. This conjecture proposes that the product's positive matching decomposition number is bounded below by the sum of those of its factors, up to an additive universal constant.
title: Additive lower-bound conjecture for positive matching decomposition numbers
technical_disposition: A universal constant must bound the pmd product defect for all factor graphs. Maximum degree is too weak when pmd exceeds degree; source HTML404 was stopped, definitions/proved bounds not body-read. No unsupported product counterfamily claimed.

statement:
Let $A$ be an abelian variety defined over a number field $K$, and let $\mathcal{L}$ be a symmetric ample line bundle on $A$. For a point $P\in A(\overline{K})$, let $D=[K(P):K]$ and let $g_0(P)$ be the dimension of the smallest algebraic subgroup of $A$ containing $P$. **Lehmer's conjecture.** There is a constant $C>0$ such that

$$
\hat{h}_{\mathcal{L}}(P)\geq C D^{-1/g_0(P)}
$$

for all non-torsion points $P\in A(\overline{K})$. This is a Lehmer-type lower bound for canonical heights on abelian varieties; the paper presents it as a conjectural application of its lower-bound results, and its resolution is not established in the supplied context.
title: Lehmer's conjecture for abelian varieties
technical_disposition: Every abelian variety and all non-torsion points require the degree-height bound with dimensiong0(P). A fixed variety/point estimate cannot produce a uniform positive constant; deep height dependencies and no bounded certificate route.

statement: Let $k\geq 3$, let $F$ be a $k$-uniform hypergraph, and let $G$ be an input $k$-uniform hypergraph. Write $\mathrm{rem}_F(G)$ for the minimum number of edges that must be removed from $G$ to make it $F$-free. A **matching** is a hypergraph whose edges are pairwise vertex-disjoint. **Hypergraph matching conjecture.** For every $k\geq 3$ and every $k$-graph $F$, computing $\mathrm{rem}_F(G)$ is polynomial-time solvable if $F$ is a matching and NP-hard otherwise.
title: Hypergraph matching conjecture for edge-modification complexity
technical_disposition: Every fixed k>=3 and F requires the algorithmic matching/nonmatching dichotomy. Finite edge-deletion optimization proves neither a polynomial algorithm for all inputs nor NP-hardness; source complexity and containment conventions unread.

statement:
For $a,b\in\{+,-\}$, a digraph is $(a,b)$-locally irregular if, for every arc $uv$, $d^a(u)\neq d^b(v)$; let $\mathrm{lir}^{(+,+)}(D)$ be the minimum number of colors in an arc coloring whose color classes are $(+,+)$-locally irregular. **Bensmail–Renault conjecture.** Every oriented graph $D$ satisfies

$$
\mathrm{lir}^{(+,+)}(D)\leq 3.
$$

The source reports that the conjecture is open, while a general upper bound of five is known for arbitrary digraphs and deciding whether the index is at most two is NP-complete.
title: Bensmail–Renault conjecture on locally irregular colorings of oriented graphs
technical_disposition: Every oriented graph requires a3-color arc decomposition with out-degree inequalities on each arc. Local recoloring changes both endpoint degrees and constraints on neighboring arcs; no all-graph discharging or exact counterexample mechanism identified.
